SC-http-miss.acceptance: An admitted miss or stale response reaches the source; cache/privacy rules are respected and the client verifies before use. Unsigned or expired metadata is rejected unless an explicit trusted-source exception was selected.

SC-http-cache-untrusted.acceptance: Cached content is verified at the client and rejected when trust fails, without a source fetch. Model trust is an input, not a cryptographic check.

SC-http-denied.acceptance: A rejected client, destination or port receives denial and the recording source sees no request.

SC-http-untrusted.acceptance: When publisher verification fails after retrieval, the client rejects the content before use. Model trust is an input, not a cryptographic check.

SC-http-source-failure.acceptance: A source failure after an admitted miss produces no usable content, no client verification and no implicit stale fallback. The execution model supplies availability; deployed failure behavior needs separate evidence.

SC-https.acceptance: An admitted CONNECT establishes source-authenticated client TLS. Encrypted payload is neither cached nor inspected; client verification still applies.
SC-https.manual: Run the Stage 1 accepted-source HTTPS retrieval on the deployed route; verify source certificate/hostname, payload integrity and refusal of invalid trust. The isolated HTTP fixture does not forward CONNECT.

SC-https-denied.acceptance: A disallowed CONNECT destination, client or port receives denial without opening a source connection.

SC-http-hit.acceptance: A repeated eligible fresh response is served without another origin request. The client still verifies trusted metadata/signatures.
